Somme Sketcher, Diana Ţuţuianu (Translator)

4.18

Am știut din prima clipă că e pericol pur.
O roșcată într-o rochie furată, cu toată lumea ei strânsă într-o geantă veche, nu poate aduce nimic bun.
A intrat în barul meu ca o furtună, cu fum în păr și păcat pe buze, și m-a provocat la un joc.
A câștigat. Mi-a luat ceasul. Și, fără să-și dea seama, mi-a luat și liniștea.
Din clipa în care a urcat treptele spre viața mea, totul s-a schimbat.
Imperiul pe care l-am ridicat s-a clătinat.
Farmecul meu calculat s-a transformat în haos.
Masca de gentleman a picat.
Dușmanii au simțit mirosul sângelui și s-au apropiat.
Poate că ghicitoarea a avut dreptate.
Regina de cupă mă va duce cu ea în iad.
Dar printre flăcări e minunat.

➳ A cartomancer told Rafe that a redheaded girl would bring him to his knees and be his doom card! Nine years later, Rafe met the redheaded little thief, aka Penny! 🤭

⤷ tropes: 🃏
* Enemies to lovers
* Office Romance
* Forced Proximity
* Touch Her & You Die
* Obsessed Hero
* Fiesty Heroine

➳ Their first interaction was hilarious, and I really enjoyed it! The banter between them was highly entertaining! Penny was full of sass, and Rafe never backed down from a challenge. 🤭

Penny (21): She is a thief and on the run for committing arson. She met Rafe at his bar and conned him into giving her his watch! Later, she works for him on his yacht as a bartender, and she believes she's lucky! 🍀

Rafe (34): He is a gentleman! Unlike his violent and impulsive brothers, he is the voice of reason, a devil hidden behind perfect suits and cufflinks! He owns the majority of the casinos and bars and is very successful! He was intrigued by Penny, but his business is going downhill, and he believes it's because of Penny and her bad luck! 😋

— Although this book was enjoyable, and I really liked the banter, what I didn't appreciate was Penny getting jealous of everyone! I understand that money is important (HELL, I understand this a lot 🥹) and that she has traumas and doesn't believe in love. However, it's still not okay to be jealous and petty over others' happiness! She regrets her past actions and is trying hard to live a better life. She's really alone and badly needs someone to confide in and thinks a lot about having friends. I mostly felt bad for her, but she's really strong! The experiences she has faced have shaped her character. Her character reminds me a lot of Georgia from "Ginny & Georgia." And Rafe! 🥹 He's so hot, I don't know 🤷🏻‍♀️ I enjoyed all his smirks and sarcasm in front of Penny! He doesn't act gentlemanly around her and is annoyed by her most of the book, but he can't stay away from her and stop being possessive! The man even punched his soldier for staring at Penny when he has never used his hands because, DUH, HE'S A GENTLEMAN! 🤭

— This book have a lot of banter! It's full of that and also height shaming lmaooooo! Penny is 5'2 and Rafe does not let her live with that fact! 😭

— It's dual POV and doesn't contain explicit sex scenes! If you're expecting a spicy book, it's not. It has a lot of sexual tension and a few bold scenes, but nothing more! 😮‍💨

— This book focused more on showing that THEY ARE ENEMIES and did not show sudden BODY BETRAYING SYNDROME, JUMPING INTO THE BED & the most popular fingerfucking. ☺️

Lastly, this book was kind of long! Not that I didn't enjoy it, but it was a little bit extra, and it's a duet! And honestly, there was no cliffhanger at the end 🙂

4 ⭐️ I flew through this one.

I genuinely couldn’t put it down. I finished it in basically a day because I needed to know what happened next. You know those books where you’d much rather keep reading than do literally anything else you’re supposed to be doing?

Yeah… this was one of them.

🃏The Premise

Nine years after a cartomancer warns him that a redheaded girl will become his doom card, Raphael Visconti comes face to face with Penny Price—a clever thief who challenges him to a game and walks away wearing his watch.

After an unexpected favor, Penny finds herself working aboard Rafe’s yacht. As the two trade bets, challenge each other at every turn, and fight an undeniable attraction, Rafe can’t ignore that his carefully controlled world seems to be falling apart from the moment she appeared.

🍀 My Thoughts

╰┈➤ Rafe & Penny

I had so much fun with these two.

The banter was easily one of my favorite parts of the book.

"That's for winning the bet." She pulls out another hundred.
"Plus VAT." She cocks her head in thought, then pulls out another.
"Plus tip."

Penny is bold, stubborn, and never afraid to challenge Rafe, while he refuses to let her get the upper hand. They’re constantly trying to outsmart each other, and I found myself grinning through so many of their interactions.

Rafe is calm, composed, and always impeccably put together… until Penny walks into the room and suddenly all that control starts slipping.

I couldn’t get enough of watching the perfect gentleman unravel whenever Penny was around.

"If I'm sinking to the bottom, at least her voice will keep me company on the way down."

And then there were the quieter moments…

The fact that he drives around all night so she can finally get some sleep? 🥹

"She was comfortable here, in my car, beside me, her hair piled on top of her head and her face make-up free. It was with a sickening sweetness that I realized she sought out the warmth of my car to do the most vulnerable thing a human can do: sleep."

Or the way they share food?

Those moments completely melted me.

╰┈➤ The Romance

The tension???
SO. GOOD.

Every lingering glance, every challenge, every conversation had me waiting for the moment one of them finally gave in.

And the stripping scene??? 🥵

I realize it's a Black Amex.
My eyes clash with Raphael's.
"Pin is four, eight, four, two," he says quietly. He locks his fingers behind his head and leans back against the headrest. His gaze flashes like a warning sign. "Now, take it off"

That said…

I spent the entire book thinking, “Okay… surely THIS is when they’re finally going to kiss.”

…and they never did. 😂

I knew going in that this was the first half of a duet and a true slow burn, so I wasn’t expecting everything to happen in book one.

Even so, after all that delicious tension, I found myself wishing for just a little more payoff before the ending.

♠️ Final Take

Overall, I had such a great time reading this. I absolutely loved Rafe and Penny, their chemistry had me hooked, and it was so much fun being back in Devil’s Dip.

Seeing Rory and Angelo again made me ridiculously happy, and the side characters continue to be one of my favorite parts of this series.

There’s absolutely no way I’m leaving these two here. Book two, here I come.

Tropes / What to Expect

🃏 Mafia Romance
🎰 Boss × Employee
🏡 Forced Proximity
🎲 Slow Burn (emphasis on slow)
♦️ 13-Year Age Gap
🔪 Touch Her and Die
🎧 Duet Narration

★★★☆☆ (3.5)
╰─ ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ───────────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ─╯

🎵 “Suffer” – Bex

✧ 𝒅𝒂𝒓𝒌 𝒓𝒐𝒎𝒂𝒏𝒄𝒆 ✧ 𝒈𝒓𝒖𝒎𝒑𝒚 𝒎𝒐𝒓𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒚 𝒈𝒓𝒂𝒚 𝒎𝒄 ✧ 𝒂𝒈𝒆𝒏𝒅𝒂-𝒇𝒊𝒍𝒍𝒆𝒅 𝒕𝒆𝒏𝒔𝒊𝒐𝒏 ✧ 𝒍𝒐𝒕𝒔 𝒐𝒇 𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒓𝒊𝒏𝒈 ✧

𓍢ִ໋🖤 𝐌𝐘 𝐑𝐄𝐀𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 𓍢ִ໋🖤

This one was a bit of a rollercoaster in the “I want to love this but why am I still on page 200 and nothing has moved” kind of way.

I gave it a 3.5 because there are things I genuinely enjoyed, but the reading experience itself felt like it kept stalling on me. The repetition and heavy focus on physical attraction made it hard for me to stay emotionally locked in, and the breaks I took definitely didn’t help the immersion either. Everything started to feel a bit disconnected instead of building steadily.

At times it felt like the story was more about vibes and staring than actual progression. Not necessarily bad vibes… just very extended ones. I definitely had moments where I considered just putting it down and letting them live in my imagination instead, where things probably would’ve moved faster.

✦ 𝐒𝐓𝐎𝐑𝐘 & 𝐒𝐓𝐀𝐑𝐓𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐏𝐎𝐈𝐍𝐓 ⋆˚📜

the setup itself is actually interesting: A cardomancer predicts that a redheaded girl will be Rafe Visconti’s downfall, his doom card.

Nine years later, that prophecy collides with Penny Price, aka the “redheaded little thief,” and suddenly everything starts spiraling into tension, games, and obsession.

✦ 𝐑𝐀𝐅𝐄 𝐕𝐈𝐒𝐂𝐎𝐍𝐓𝐈 ⋆˚🖤

Rafe is honestly the strongest part of the book for me.

Dark, broody, dangerous, but packaged in a perfectly controlled gentleman façade that does not hold up the moment Penny enters his orbit.

He’s the type of MMC who is calm for the world but absolutely unhinged when it comes to her. Like there is no middle ground. It’s either “businessman in a suit” or “I will end you where you stand.”

⤷#🪻The gun habit in this family is consistent

What I did like is how obsessive his attention becomes in such small, quiet ways. The way he drives around just so she can sleep, how easily she becomes the center of his focus even when he’s pretending she’s not.

★ “Just because I’m a gentleman, Penelope, doesn’t always mean I’m a gentle man.” ★
That line basically is him.

His tension with her? actually electric. The problem is it stays electric for so long without fully releasing into anything that feels like payoff.
Still I get the appeal. He’s the kind of MMC you don’t casually read, you endure him.

✦ 𝐏𝐄𝐍𝐍𝐘 𝐏𝐑𝐈𝐂𝐄 ⋆˚🌹

Penny is chaotic in a very fun way.

She’s fearless, stubborn, and absolutely committed to making bad decisions on purpose if it means she gets to win the game. I liked that energy a lot, she doesn’t just exist in the story, she actively pushes against it.

But I’ll be honest I didn’t feel super deeply connected to her as a character. I understood her, I enjoyed her actions, but I didn’t get a strong emotional anchor with her.

She’s more “watch her do something insane” than “deep emotional attachment,” at least for me.

★ “I said I’d rather shit in my hands and clap than hit on you.” ★
She deserves a medal for that alone saying that to a VISCONTI

✦ 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐑𝐎𝐌𝐀𝐍𝐂𝐄 ⋆˚🖤

The tension was INSANE. genuinely one of the strongest parts of the book. The problem is the pacing of it.

It’s very much slow burn taken to its absolute limit, but not in a way that always feels like it’s building toward something. More like staring contests that last several chapters.

There were moments where I fully understood the chemistry and even felt that after all this lust and almost no control when seeing the other, you would think that something would happen sometime now.

But then it circles back again into lingering looks, repeated attraction focus, and not enough emotional development to match the intensity being described. It felt more like lust-heavy obsession than a balanced emotional arc.

I really wanted to like this after seeing all of the good things said about this book, and my experience with the first book. 🥹

✦ 𝐏𝐋𝐎𝐓 & 𝐏𝐀𝐂𝐈𝐍𝐆 ⋆˚🌫️

This is where I struggled the most.
The idea is strong, the setup is interesting, and the characters have potential, but the actual movement of the story felt stretched.

At almost 450 pages, it often felt like not much was actually happening, just being prolonged. I found myself losing immersion and needing breaks, which made the repetition stand out even more. I genuinely think part of my reaction might also be timing, But this one didn’t hit the same emotional or narrative momentum for me.

✦ 𝐅𝐈𝐍𝐀𝐋 𝐓𝐇𝐎𝐔𝐆𝐇𝐓𝐒 ⋆˚⭐

I didn’t hate it. Not even close.
There are parts I really enjoyed, especially Rafe’s character, the tension, and some of the banter-heavy moments between him and Penny.

But overall, it felt too long for the amount of actual progression, and too focused on surface-level attraction instead of deeper emotional build. I finished it feeling a bit disappointed because I could see what it wanted to be I just didn’t fully feel it land.

After all those pages, I honestly have no idea what’s going to happen in the second book 🥹

Rating: 4.5 stars.
OH. MY. GOD. This book literally SHOCKED me in the best way possible. I wasn’t expecting it to be this good, and honestly? I’m flattered, obsessed, and completely speechless all at once. Like… why didn’t I read this sooner?? I’ve been hunting for the perfect romance for ages, forgetting that dark romance is where the true yearning men live, and this book delivered in every single way.

This is exactly what I mean by slow burn: tension that makes you ache, chemistry that explodes off every page, a gradual, simmering love that grips your chest… but let me tell you, SLOW BURN, but make it EVEN SLOWER because AHHHHH. I was living for every second of this, and not a single crumb was left behind. And whoever said the “made series” is better than THIS? No. Absolutely NOT. I ate this up, savored every line, and I am officially obsessed. But I really wanted to enjoy that series, eventually it was just cringe characters and couldn't bare them.

── .✦

Okay, first of all… I literally don’t even know where to start because this book COMPLETELY wrecked me and left me absolutely shook, but in the best way imaginable. I went in thinking I was getting a spicy, dark, dangerous romance with just a hint of chaos… and oh honey, Somme Sketcher didn’t just give me a hint, she unleashed a full-on hurricane of emotions, tension, and fire that had me screaming internally. I’m completely obsessed. Every nerve in my body was on high alert, my heart racing, palms sweating, and jaw literally on the floor. I couldn’t tear my eyes away for a single second, fangirling so hard that I almost forgot to breathe. This story? It’s a full-throttle, all-consuming ride, and I am here for every second of it.

── .✦

Oh my god, the characters! I won't talk much let's just dive into them!

°˖➴ Penny Price:
"This girl isn’t the Queen of Hearts, but the Devil in disguise.
Unfortunately, I can’t say for sure I wouldn’t follow her into hell."
OH. MY. GOD. Penny Price is literally EVERYTHING!! She’s bold, sassy, and wickedly clever, the kind of heroine who makes you scream “YASS QUEEN!” every single time she outsmarts everyone around her. I was living for her fearless energy and that unstoppable spark she brings to every scene. Sure, she gets herself into trouble sometimes, but honestly? That just makes her even more badass and impossible not to root for. I swear, she’s the kind of girl you’d want as your bestie while lowkey fangirling over her every move. And the BEST part? Beneath that strong, untouchable exterior is this emotional depth that hits you without warning. I literally didn’t blink when she spoke or acted, and that, my friends, is peak FMC love.

°˖➴ Rafe Viscouti:
“Why do you care if I cry?”
“Because last night, I saw you laugh.”
And Rafe Visconti… ohhhhhh, don’t even get me started. Dark, broody, dangerous… but also with these hidden layers that make your heart melt like butter. I love that he’s this gentleman to the world, but with her? Yeah… let’s just say he’s a whole different level.

he’s that gorgeous, powerful, cashmere-charm-wrapping, gentlemanly façade type, whose world completely unravels the moment she shows up. I mean, my empire started crumbling just reading it. His calm, control, and subtle dominance versus her wild, fearless energy? Absolute fire. The tension, the banter, the unspoken threats and desires, every scene felt electric, like I was sitting in a storm and loving every second.

── .✦

The tension between them? OH, IT’S OFF THE CHARTS. Every glance lingers too long, every word drips with unspoken meaning, and every subtle touch feels electric. I was gripping my book, my heart racing, just from the way they moved around each other. Their dynamic is a perfect storm, messy, fiery, and utterly intoxicating. It’s the kind of chemistry that makes you sigh, swoon, and simultaneously panic because you just KNOW the consequences of their feelings are going to be explosive. Every scene together had me internally screaming, fangirling like mad, and craving more. Together, they destroy and rebuild each other in the most addictive, heart-stopping way imaginable, and I am 100% obsessed.

Also… can we talk about the utter chaos she brings? She’s lucky, yes, but the kind of luck that drags him through flames, forces him to face enemies closing in, and still makes me giggle and scream at the same time. Queen of Hearts indeed.

── .✦

The Writing:
And the writing? Absolute perfection. Darkly seductive, sharp, and addictively twisted, it pulls you in from the first line. Every sentence drips with tension, every small power move hits like a thrill, and every quiet moment between them leaves you craving more. It’s intoxicating, messy, and utterly satisfying, like the author knew exactly how to keep your heart racing and your mind hooked.

The Story:
What truly caught me off guard is how rich and layered this story is. It’s not just a romance; it delves into the complexities of two people struggling with their past mistakes, the weight of control over their lives and others, and the sacrifices they make for loyalty and trust. Every interaction carries emotional depth, and the tension isn’t just romantic, it’s woven into their very decisions, their fears, and their sense of responsibility. This adds a whole other level of intensity that keeps you completely hooked, feeling everything alongside them.

Wow. Such a good surprise. After reading the first book and being really disappointed with it, I wasn’t expecting this! I am shocked over my current obsession with these two!

If i’m sinking to the bottom, at least her voice will keep me company on the way down.

╰┈➤ 9 years ago a cartomancer told Raphael to choose between the king of diamonds or the king of hearts, and he chose business over love. But his reading foresees a doom card where a red head will bring him down to his knees and crumble his empire. Fast forward to the present when Rafe meets the lucky Penny who swindles him from his watch and later comes to work for him. Amidst wild banter and games the tension between the two rises while Raphael’s empire slowly falls, all because of his doomed Queen of Hearts.

What you’re signing up for:
💋 Mafia romance
🃏 Enemies to lovers vibes
♥️ Boss x Employee
🔪 Touch her and die
♦️ Age gap
🎲 Slowest of burns

You know when you read a book that objectively isn’t the best but then gives you all the butterflies and feels, makes you giggle uncontrollably and gasp over the faintest of touches? Yep, this is that book for me! I don’t think it has the best plot but the romance has me in a chokehold!!

“You sure are persistent for a man that isn’t interested.” His gaze drops to my mouth.
“Oh, I’m interested.”

I don’t think it’s a true enemies to lovers but it gives off those vibes and angsty banter so well! From literally the first scene when Penny swindles Rafe their connection is off the charts! Ughhhh and then all the little games they played and bets they made accompanied by the best banter just to try and one up each other!!! 😩 Intensity done well!! I swear they had the best interactions! And the slow burn is scrumptious!!! The way Somme writes the scenes with the best kind of sexual tension without nothing even happening is gold! I was sweating over a few grazes and heated glances, I can’t even describe it. They are so hot and have the best chemistry ever!!! That car scene IYKYK 🥵🥵

“Bet you’ll kiss me first.”
“Bet you a million dollars my lips would never touch yours first.”
“You don’t have a million dollars.”
“Doesn’t matter, because I’m not going to lose.”

𐙚—♥️ Penny is such a great character. Nothing like annoying Rory from the first book! She has a dark past but is still so strong and striving to do her best and keep her head above water. She’s feisty, bratty, mouthy, sexy and has the best comebacks!

“Why do you care if I cry?”
“Because last night, I saw you laugh.”

𐙚—🎲 RAPHAEL VISCONTI!!!! Oh my gosh, I’m in love! Instantly obsessed! Unlike his brothers he doesn’t get his hands bloodied because he’s a gentleman, unless it comes to her! Because he doesn’t act like a gentleman around her and if someone even looks at her the wrong way he’s not afraid to get blood on his hands!

“Just because I'm a gentleman, Penelope, doesn't always mean I'm a gentle man.”

Ughhh he’s just so hot with all his smirking and sarcasm! He makes the simplest thing look like the hottest thing ever! (talking specifically when he demonstrated very not sexually how to open a champagne bottle! Deceased was my status after reading that! 🫠) AND HIS MOUTH, don’t even!!

“Strip for another man again, and he’ll die crossing the road.”

The plot could be so much better though! Just like with the first book there’s a lot of potential, especially after how things ended but nothing much is done with that. I just wish there was a better balance between plot and romance. If I wasn’t so invested in the characters this would’ve been a miss.

“Or maybe I just want to see you shut your dick in a car door.”
“Or maybe you just want to see my dick.”

And for the part that really grates my nerves: why the hell did the author completely change the plot with Penny and Rafe from the first book to this one? Let me explain. In the last chapter of Sinners anonymous Angelo sees a red head who’s doing a terrible job at being a waitress and approaches her to fire her, she tries to run and in comes Rafe. Even though they don’t say her name it’s made pretty obvious from the interactions between them that it’s Penny. And besides this Angelo says she’s the one who sold him the fortune cookie. And then in the second book this whole plot is erased and swapped. I understand that after writing it maybe the author wanted to write a different first meeting, but she could still’ve done that and still have this scene! Honestly I think it could’ve been even better in some ways. I was so annoyed because I was waiting for it and it never came. And what pissed me off even more was the fact that she and Angelo apparently never met. Ugh it could’ve been such an interesting plot. I was able to look past it and still love the book, but I still wanted to address this massive plot hole because I never see anyone talking about it. I mean, is my book different?

Also, I don’t understand why this is a duet. If there was a plot that needed development or something happened between them I could’ve understood the decision for it. But there isn’t even a cliffhanger!!!

Still, this is such an amazing romance, that’s sure to leave you ultimately yearning for more in the end!

4 Play a Game With Me Stars ⭐

You could say it's an evenly matched game of cat & mouse. She's mouthy and bratty and in so much trouble that Penny no longer recognises the right way up. Everytime she swears it's the last, there's one more temptation. The perfect thief in a pretty package. Until she trys to con the conman. This will be the biggest risk of them all.

This girl isn’t the Queen of Hearts, but the Devil in disguise. Unfortunately, I can’t say for sure I wouldn’t follow her into hell.

Rafe Visconti is a gentleman, well that's the perception. He stopped getting blood on his hands years ago. But only an idiot would mistake his persona for weakness. He's mafia through and through. The king of casinos, gambling and games. Until he meets Lady Luck or is it possibly doom?

The chemistry and instant connection over the first swindle is intense. As they try to one up each other, you know it's the beginning of a tumultuous affair. Every encounter feels inevitable and every interaction is a wager, never knowing who will triumph.

The issue with a duet that ends in a cliffhanger means you either get a flushed out story or a fair bit of waffling, and Sinners Condemned was the latter. It's true that this series is slow burn Mafia romance (and it really is) and there was too much tension, not enough action in my opinion. I could of used more sex! However, I can't epmhasise enough how good the witty dialogue is! It's fucking top notch.

𝐇𝐢𝐬 𝐠𝐚𝐳𝐞 𝐝𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐦𝐲 𝐦𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐡. "𝐎𝐡, 𝐈'𝐦 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝."

SO GOOD. I haven't read a mafia series that I liked in a while, but this has just became an all time favorite. Rafe and Penny are everything. If you like The Made Men Series by Danielle Lori, you'll love this. Honestly, it was even better and that's a bold statement since I LOVE The Made Men. If you didn't enjoy book 1, you'll enjoy this one much more.

This book follows Rafe, brother to Angelo, and Penny, a friend of Rory's who returns home to Devil's Cove after an incident in Atlantic City. Penny has been on her own since her parents died, conning rich men and doing whatever it takes to survive. When she runs into Rafe one night in attempt to con him out of his expensive watch, there is no denying the attraction (and fear) she has for him. Eventually, she gets hired at one of his casinos and their relationship develops from there.

This is your typical "MMC denies his attraction towards the FMC, but eventually realizes he's obsessed with her" trope. Rafe acts as if he doesn't want her, but deep down, he knows Penny is his weakness. Their tension throughout this whole book was so, so good and was written incredibly well. I found myself giggling and smiling at how much they flirted with each other. Penny is a strong character and isn't afraid to stand up for herself. Loved her personality and how well she matches Rafe. We also get to see Rory and Angelo in this book (I absolutely adored the little snippets of them) and the relationship that Rory built with the Visconti family. This book also picked up a lot faster than book 1, which I think warrants a second chance if you didn't like book 1.

I cannot wait for Sinners Consumed and to read the rest of Rafe and Penny's story. This had all of my favorite tropes. Seriously - READ THIS SERIES!!

Tropes:
-Age gap (FMC is 21, MMC is 34)
-Mafia romance
-Small town romance
-Slow burn + a touch of enemies to lovers
-So. Much. Tension.

I already enjoyed Sinners Annonymous so much, but I felt like i loved Rafe and Penny even more. And Rafe? That man is pure fire. He likes to uphold that ice-cold facade, but don't be fooled, there's a devil inside and he's breaking loose.
